title: Document Structure: Headings & Landmarks 📐
description: Master heading hierarchy and landmark regions to create a navigable page skeleton.

slides.title: Headings Are a Table of Contents 📑
slides.content:
Screen reader users navigate by headings. A proper hierarchy is critical.

* Use **only one `<h1>`** per page – the main title.
* Nest headings logically: `<h2>` under `<h1>`, `<h3>` under `<h2>`.
* Never skip levels (h1 → h3) just for visual size.

**Visual size ≠ heading level.** Use CSS for sizing, keep the hierarchy semantic.

quizData.question:
What is wrong with `

Title

Subtitle

`?

options.text: Headings should never be different sizes
A heading level is skipped (h1 to h3, missing h2)

quizData.explanation: Skipping levels confuses the logical outline. The next heading after an h1 should be h2.

slides.title: Landmarks: The Page’s Skeleton 🏛️
slides.content:
Semantic structural elements automatically create **landmark regions**. Screen readers can jump to them.

* `<header>` (when not inside `<article>` or `<section>`)
* `<nav>` – navigation
* `<main>` – primary content (only one per page)
* `<footer>`
* `<aside>` – complementary content
* `<section>` and `<article>` (when given an accessible name)

**Always wrap your main content in `<main>`.**

quizData.question: Which element automatically creates a 'main' landmark?
quizData.explanation: The `<main>` element maps to the main landmark role, indicating the primary content of the page.

slides.title: The 'Skip Navigation' Link 🔗
slides.content:
Even with landmarks, keyboard users appreciate a **skip link** that jumps straight to `
`. * First focusable element on the page. * Becomes visible on focus. * Example: ```html Skip to main content ```

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Validate with a Screen Reader
Open VoiceOver rotor (CapsLock+U) and select 'Landmarks'. You'll see all regions. If they're messy, your HTML is too.
